title: Reusable context manager
prompt:
Implement `class Timer` usable as a context manager AND reusable across runs:

- `with Timer() as t:` — on exit, `t.elapsed` is a float ≥ 0 seconds
- `t.runs` counts completed blocks
- nested usage of two Timers must be independent
- entering must return the timer itself

tests.name: measures a block once
tests.code:
t = Timer()
with t:
    time.sleep(0.01)
assert t.elapsed >= 0.01, f'elapsed={t.elapsed}'
assert t.runs == 1
print('ok')
tests.hint: __exit__ receives (exc_type, exc, tb); return False/None so exceptions still propagate.

tests.name: reusable and independent
tests.code:
t = Timer()
with t:
    pass
with t:
    time.sleep(0.005)
assert t.runs == 2

a, b = Timer(), Timer()
with a:
    with b:
        pass
assert a.runs == 1 and b.runs == 1
assert b.elapsed < a.elapsed or b.elapsed >= 0
print('ok')
tests.hint: Reset the clock in __enter__, finalize in __exit__.
